title: Warning Signs of High Cholesterol You Can’t Feel
description: 95% of adults with LDL >160 have no symptoms — discover why eye checks, ankle pulses, and family history matter most.
perplexityQuestions: What are the symptoms of high cholesterol in adults over 35, and can it go unnoticed for years?
Is an LDL of 130, 160, or 190 dangerous at age 40, 45, or 50 if I otherwise feel healthy?
What does it mean if my total cholesterol is under 200 but my LDL is still high?
Can high cholesterol be genetic even if I eat well and exercise?
Should I ask for an ApoB or lipoprotein(a) test if my cholesterol is borderline high at 35+?
competitorCoverage: Top-ranking adult cholesterol articles usually explain what cholesterol is, the difference between LDL, HDL, and triglycerides, common causes and risk factors, and how testing works and how often to screen.[1][2][3][4][7][9] To compete, a new article should also cover risk-stratified thresholds by age and condition, advanced tests like ApoB and lipoprotein(a), when lifestyle changes are not enough, and clear guidance on when medication is typically discussed.[3][7][8][9]
